name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
description: The federal definition: a two- or three-wheeled vehicle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, which the motor alone can't propel at 20 mph. It makes an e-bike a consumer product, regulated like a bicycle by the Consumer Product Safety Commission rather than as a motor vehicle; states decide where and how it's ridden.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts (1 hp)
On the motor alone, its top speed on a paved level surface with a 170-pound rider is under 20 mph; the limit doesn't apply to speed reached while pedaling
A consumer product, not a motor vehicle: meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) instead of federal motor vehicle safety standards, with no VIN
One more powerful or faster on the motor alone isn't a low-speed electric bicycle, and federal motor vehicle rules can apply to it
Overrides any state product requirement stricter than the federal one; states still set the rules for riding it
Federal law sets no minimum age, helmet, license, registration or insurance requirement

On a federally funded trail or pedestrian walkway, the only motorized vehicle allowed besides maintenance vehicles, snowmobiles and wheelchairs, and only where state or local rules permit; there an e-bike is Class 1, 2 or 3 with a motor under 750 watts

In national parks: allowed on park roads, parking areas, and administrative roads and trails open to bicycles, only where the superintendent designates; there it's not a motor vehicle, and state law governs its use
In national parks, riding on the motor alone without pedaling for an extended time is prohibited except where public motor vehicles are allowed
Banned from federally designated wilderness areas

On Bureau of Land Management, Fish and Wildlife Service and Bureau of Reclamation lands, treated as a bicycle rather than a motorized vehicle where the authorized officer allows e-bikes on nonmotorized trails

On national forests and grasslands, a motor vehicle: all three classes may ride roads and trails open to motor vehicles, and a nonmotorized trail only where the Forest Service designates it for e-bikes
